# Draft:Tom Howard

----
Thomas "Tom" Howard (born April 1996) is a British neurodiversity and autism awareness campaigner based in Bury St Edmunds, Suffolk. He is known for advocacy on behalf of autistic and other neurodivergent people in education and society across the UK. Howard founded a community cinema project to make film screenings accessible and has led national petitions on disability rights issues. His work has featured in local and national media, including Bury Free Press, The Canary, and BBC Radio Suffolk. Howard was born in Harleston, Norfolk, and was diagnosed with autism while at university, an experience that later fuelled his campaigns.
Advocacy and campaigns
Neurodiversity training in higher education
In April 2023, Howard launched a petition urging the UK Government to require all university staff to receive training on neurodiversity. Motivated by his own university experiences, where he struggled to obtain reasonable adjustments and did not complete his degree, the petition argued mandatory staff training was necessary to improve inclusion. The petition, titled "Require Universities to Train Staff on Neurodiversity," gained 16,803 signatures over six months and received a formal government response. In November 2023, it was discussed in a Westminster Hall parliamentary debate, where it was specifically noted by MPs. Independent media such as The Canary also covered the campaign extensively.
Disability cost-of-living support
In late 2023, Howard campaigned to reinstate the Disability Cost of Living Payment after the UK government discontinued the £150 supplemental payment. Arguing the payment was essential due to higher living costs faced by disabled people, he launched a Change.org petition in December 2023, which quickly amassed over 70,000 signatures. Howard delivered the petition to 10 Downing Street in February 2024, gaining significant media coverage and support from charities such as Epilepsy Action.
Community projects and Bury Film Group CIC
Howard founded the Bury Film Group CIC in 2023, incorporated officially in September 2024, to provide autism-friendly cinema screenings. These free, accessible screenings aimed to foster inclusion for neurodivergent individuals and those facing financial barriers. Howard has also led other community projects, such as creating inclusive Halloween "treat bags" for children unable to participate traditionally and organising local volunteer litter-picking events.
Political involvement
Howard served as Deputy Campaign Organiser for Labour's Dr Peter Prinsley during the 2024 General Election for the Bury St Edmunds and Stowmarket constituency. Following Prinsley’s election victory, Howard became his Constituency Support Manager, overseeing local community engagement and constituency casework. He also holds roles within the local Labour Party, including Disability Officer, promoting accessibility in politics.
Awards and recognition
Howard received the Personal Achievement Award at the Autism Hero Awards in March 2025, organised by the charity Anna Kennedy Online. In 2024, he was named one of The Big Issue’s Top 100 Changemakers. Locally, he won the Good Deed Award (2023) and Most Helpful Neighbour Award (2024) at the Bury Free Press Community Awards.
